nodes.name: CrNN
aliases: nanoscale Ni metal cores over-coated by a Cr2O3-blended NiO layer

nodes.name: CrNN Synthesis on Ni Foam
nodes.procedure: The catalyst was synthesized by hydrolysis of precursors at 90°C, drop-drying the product to coat a Ni foam followed by annealing at 300°C. Ni powder (30 wt%) was intentionally added during drop drying of reaction precursors into a Ni foam.

unit_operations.name: Drop-drying with Ni powder
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: drop-drying the product to coat a Ni foam... We intentionally added Ni powder during drop drying

nodes.source_text: The catalyst was synthesized by hydrolysis of precursors at 90°C, drop-drying the product to coat a Ni foam followed by annealing at 300°C (see the Supporting Information). We intentionally added Ni powder during drop drying of reaction precursors into a Ni foam.

nodes.description: HER LSV comparison in 1 M KOH (Figure 2a)
nodes.source_text: In 1m KOH, the CrNN electrocatalyst showed zero overpotential at the HER onset and 150 mV overpotential to reach a current density of 100 mA cm⁻² without iR compensation, which is similar to commercial Pt/C under similar loading (Figure 2 a)
10% Cr₂O₃ greatly stabilized the catalyst with an initially increasing current density through an activation phase over 48 h and a stable current density afterwards (Figure 2 b)
NiO/Ni electrocatalyst showed a gradual decrease in current density suggesting catalyst degradation

nodes.description: HER optimized loading with 30 wt% Ni powder
nodes.source_text: optimal loading of 24 mg cm⁻² CrNN catalyst with 30 wt% Ni powder... could yield a current density of 100 mA cm⁻² at an overpotential of 115 mV without iR compensation

nodes.description: HER long-term stability at -250 mV vs RHE
nodes.source_text: the catalyst also exhibited stable behavior in maintaining current density over 200 mA cm⁻² for at least 80 h at -250 mV versus RHE without iR compensation

nodes.description: Overall water splitting electrolyzer RT with NiFe LDH (Figure 4b)
nodes.source_text: At room temperature (RT, 23°C), the electrolyzer impressively delivered a water splitting current at an onset voltage of 1.46 V, and a high current density of 200 mA cm⁻² at 1.75 V without iR compensation (1.57 V with iR compensation; Figure 4 b)

nodes.description: Overall water splitting electrolyzer 60°C with NiFe LDH (Figure 4b)
nodes.source_text: At 60°C, the curves shifted by 100 mV to lower voltages with a 1.39 V onset potential and 1.64 V at the current density of 200 mA cm⁻²

nodes.description: Electrolyzer chronopotentiometry stability at 20 mA/cm² RT (Figure 4c)
nodes.source_text: The electrolyzer was stable at a current density of 20 mA cm⁻² under a nearly constant voltage of 1.50 V (without iR compensation) over 500 h (Figure 4 c)

nodes.description: HER stability test at -60 mV vs RHE for structural analysis
nodes.source_text: the CrNN catalyst showed negligible particle oxidation with an almost intact NiO/Ni core structure after 48 h electrolysis operation at -60 mV versus reversible hydrogen electrode

nodes.description: HER stability test for structural analysis
nodes.source_text: The NiO/Ni heterostructures without any Cr added showed significant particle oxidation into larger NiO aggregates over 24 h HER operation
By comparing the peak areas of Ni²⁺/Niᵟ⁺ redox peak before and after 48 h of HER reaction, we observed a slightly increased electrochemical surface area by 1.23 times for the CrNN electrocatalyst
It also showed negligible decay under a high current density of 200 mA cm⁻² for 50 h under 1.75 V
negligible decay under a high current density of 200 mA cm⁻² for 50 h under ... 1.64 V at RT and 60°C, respectively
we were able to produce a high current density of 12.10 mA cm⁻² corresponding to a solar-to-hydrogen efficiency of 14.9% under AM1.5 100 mW cm⁻²
under lower power density of 20 mW cm⁻² by LED desk light, the device could still deliver a current density of 2.45 mA cm⁻² corresponding to a solar-to-hydrogen efficiency of 15.1%

nodes.characterization_summary: High-magnification STEM-EELS chemical maps show 3-10 nm metallic Ni cores coated by 1-2 nm NiOx partitioned by 1-2 nm CrOx domains forming Cr2O3-blended NiO/Ni heterostructures; structure remains intact after stability test while NiO/Ni shows severe oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic scale electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) mapping... revealed 3-10 nm metallic Ni cores coated by a 1–2 nm thick layer of nickel oxide (NiOx) partitioned by 1–2 nm chromium oxide (CrOx) domains (Figure 1 c–f)

nodes.characterization_summary: Depth profiling XPS confirms +2 oxidation state of Ni and +3 of Cr in oxide layer, metallic Ni core after Ar sputtering (Figure S2); intact chemical property after stability test (Figure S4).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Depth profiling X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) further confirmed the +2 and +3 oxidation states of Ni and Cr, respectively, in the oxide layer... (Figure S2). The intact NiO/Ni chemical property was further confirmed by XPS analysis (Figure S4)

nodes.characterization_summary: CV (10 mV s-1, second cycle) shows larger Ni2+/Niδ+ (δ≥3) redox peak area for CrNN vs NiO/Ni indicating larger ECSA; after 48h HER CrNN ECSA increases 1.23x with split peaks indicating two Ni2+ species while NiO/Ni ECSA decreases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: larger electrochemical surface area of the CrNN catalyst as indicated by the larger Ni2+/Niδ+ (δ≥3) redox peak area (Figure 3 c and f)... By comparing the peak areas of Ni2+/Niδ+ (δ≥3) redox peak before and after 48 h of HER reaction, we observed a slightly increased electrochemical surface area by 1.23 times
